description: Workload profiles for personal-ai-assistant-sizer bake-offs. Each profile exercises a distinct prefill/decode shape that Skippy encounters in production. The bake-off script fires N samples per profile per model and records host_ms / prefill_ms / decode_ms / prompt_tokens / completion_tokens. See CLAUDE.md and project_personal_ai_sizer.md for context.

profiles.description: Conversational single-turn, no RAG. Dominated by system prompt + persona. Measures: TTFT and steady-state decode tok/s at minimum prefill.
prompts: Hey Skippy, how's it going today?
What time is it where you are?
Tell me a short joke about embedded systems.
If I tell you my name is Kyle, what should I expect from you?
Give me a one-sentence definition of 'cache coherency'.

profiles.description: Retrieval-augmented Q&A over Skippy's 61K-doc knowledge base. Dominated by long prefill (retrieved chunks). Measures: prefill throughput + end-to-end with retrieval overhead.
prompts: What memory interface does the i.MX 93 support for external DRAM?
Which peripheral on the i.MX 93 handles UART, and what IP block routes its pins?
What Arm cores does the i.MX 93 application processor include?
In Kyle's pillar-to-pillar IVI demo, which NXP chip ran Angry Birds on the LCD?
Summarize what NXP-adjacent podcasts have said about the sustainability argument for electric vehicles.
What configurations are available for the eIQ Neutron NPU in the i.MX 95?

profiles.description: Document generation task — spec / proposal / report body. Short-to-medium prefill, very long decode. Measures: steady-state decode tok/s (dominates wall-clock).
prompts: Compose the following document below as plain text in your reply. Do not call any tools; respond with the proposal text directly. Document: a 1500-word technical proposal for integrating an on-device AI assistant into an industrial IoT gateway, covering use cases, hardware requirements, model selection, RAG architecture, deployment risks, and a 6-month rollout plan. Use section headers.

Draft a thorough engineering spec for a real-time object-detection pipeline running on an embedded NPU. Cover: input formats, model architecture choices, quantization strategy, latency budget, fallback behavior on NPU failure, telemetry, and acceptance criteria. Target ~1500 words.

Produce a detailed internal report on the tradeoffs between MoE and dense LLMs for edge deployment. Include: memory bandwidth implications, active vs total parameters, quality-vs-latency curves, and practical recommendations for sub-8GB memory budgets. ~1500 words with section headers.

profiles.description: Summarize a long transcript into action items and key points. Prefill-dominated (transcript fills most of context). Decode is short/medium. Measures: prefill throughput (dominates total wall-clock).

prompts.template:
Below is a transcript of a technical planning meeting. Produce (1) a concise summary in 3-4 sentences, (2) a bulleted list of decisions made, (3) a bulleted list of action items with owners if mentioned, and (4) any open questions flagged for follow-up.

TRANSCRIPT:
{transcript}

Now produce the summary.

transcript_synth.topic: Edge AI product planning — NPU tier selection, model choice between dense and MoE, deployment roadmap, customer feasibility

prompts.template:
Below is a transcript of a multi-team engineering sync. Output: (1) a 4-sentence summary, (2) decisions made, (3) blockers identified, (4) action items with owners and rough deadlines.

TRANSCRIPT:
{transcript}

Produce the summary now.

transcript_synth.topic: Cross-functional retrospective covering product, engineering, and customer-success views on a recent release. Includes discussion of metrics, incidents, and next-sprint priorities.

profiles.description: Single roundtrip of an agentic tool-use loop — LLM reads a tool result and emits a structured action + brief reasoning. The sizer models total agentic latency as (prefill_i + decode_i) × roundtrip_count, so this measures ONE roundtrip's cost. Prefill grows per iteration in real use; this profile samples mid-loop state.
